A mirrored root carries its transitive closure and its exact-spec reference, so spec-driven `pull` works from the mirror; manifests move as raw verified bytes, so digests survive the copy even for foreign-produced content. For the air gap, mirror into a directory, `tar` it, carry it across, untar, and set `INSPECT_RANGES_REGISTRY` to the directory: the consuming session is then identical to the connected one. A whole-location mirror carries the source’s catalog list verbatim, replacing the destination’s: names published only at the destination stay served by ref but drop out of enumeration and pin generation, so merge-style syncs between two publishing locations should republish rather than mirror. Whole-location mirroring enumerates the source’s catalog listing; the public hub does not expose org enumeration through the OCI API, so whole-org mirrors from the hub name their artifacts explicitly (the published catalog list is a recorded follow-up of the catalog phase).

## Reclaiming space: `images prune --chains`

`images prune` reports and reclaims superseded realized images, stranded capture and pull temps, and orphan sidecars; `--chains` extends it to goldens and vendor bases nothing references. Eviction is by whole chain, never a backing out from under a dependent: a golden survives while any realized image, build manifest, or live project names it, and a vendor base survives while any surviving golden’s provenance does. Reports by default; `--yes` deletes.

`inspect-ranges doctor` carries the Distribution rows: configured locations parse (directory forms must be valid layouts), and the cache’s provenance chains are whole, with broken backing references named.

## Fleet guidance for Docker Hub

Anonymous hub pulls are rate-limited per address (measured 2026-10-18: 100 pulls per rolling hour), so a fleet cold-pulling the public org should prepend its own registry (connected: bases fall through to the org only once) or mirror the org (disconnected, or to remove the hub availability dependency). One operational note for hosts logged into the hub with a narrowly-scoped access token: the docker CLI sends the stored credential for public pulls too, and the hub rejects an insufficiently-scoped token rather than falling back to anonymous, so public `docker pull`s fail on such a host. The distribution client is unaffected (it authenticates only where it must), but host provisioning that pulls public images should account for it.


# Image Catalog – Inspect Ranges

## Overview

The catalog is the set of standard images published at the project location (`docker.io/meridianlabsai/inspect-ranges`; the third segment is the hub form’s repo-name prefix, so name `attack` lives in the repo `meridianlabsai/inspect-ranges-attack` while specs keep writing the bare name), each consumable by bare name from any `image:` line and pinned by digest end to end. It gives the schema’s long-standing promises real referents: “the backend’s standard attack image” is the published `attack`, and the blessed goldens are published under the names ranges already use.

Nothing about the catalog is special-cased: these are ordinary distribution artifacts (see [Distribution](./distribution.html.md)), published with `inspect-ranges publish`, resolved pin first, then the local cache, then the search path, whose default tail is the public org. A deployment that prepends its own registry shadows any catalog name deterministically.

## The attack image

`attack` is the standard attack box: a kali-class toolset built by a pinned recipe over the noble golden, with metasploit from its official apt repository (release key pinned by fingerprint). The toolset: nmap, netcat/socat, curl/wget, tcpdump, python3 with impacket and requests, sqlmap, hydra, john, gobuster, ffuf, smbclient, ldap-utils, dnsutils, and metasploit-framework (6.x floor, asserted at build).

A dedicated attack box that declares no `image:` boots it by default. Two properties are enforced at build time and verifiable in the running image:

- **The recorded manifest.** `/etc/attack-image.manifest` records every delivered package and version plus the metasploit version: what this exact image contains, independent of what the upstream feeds have since moved to.
- **Zero non-loopback listeners.** The image refuses to build if anything listens beyond loopback, because the verification engine attributes versions through listeners and an attack box must present nothing to attack.

## The goldens and the daemon bundle

`ubuntu-noble` and `ubuntu-focal` publish as golden chains (image, provenance sidecar, vendor base), each with the guest control daemon baked in. Pulled goldens are sticky: builds keep resolving the cached artifact until an explicit `images refresh` moves the whole chain forward.

The daemon bundle publishes under the reserved `daemon-bundle` ref, so a fleet that derives its own goldens fetches the artifact instead of building it from the Go toolchain:

``` bash
$ inspect-ranges daemon-bundle --pull -o dist/daemon
```

It also travels with whole-location mirrors, so air-gapped fleets derive goldens too.

## The hardened range container image

The range container publishes as a conventional Docker image (`meridianlabsai/inspect-ranges-range`). Consumption is the digest pin described in [Distribution](./distribution.html.md#the-hardened-range-container-image): set `INSPECT_RANGES_RANGE_IMAGE` to the published `repo@sha256:` reference and `up` pulls it once and boots every range inside it; unset, the local build remains the default.

## Consuming the catalog

An eval needs no explicit fetch verbs: init pulls whatever the range resolves that is absent from the cache (the published build for a built range, catalog images otherwise), with docker-pull-shaped progress, and warm evals cost zero network. `INSPECT_RANGES_NEVER_PULL=1` turns every implicit transfer into a coded refusal for hosts that must stay offline.

Fleets pin: `inspect-ranges images pin --from docker.io/meridianlabsai/inspect-ranges --out pins.json` records every catalog name’s current root digest, and a host running with `INSPECT_RANGES_PIN_FILE` set lands exactly the pinned roots, refusing `pin-mismatch` when the first location serving a name no longer serves its pinned root (resolution aborts rather than falling through, the same posture as the search path).

## The republish discipline

Published bytes never change under a name silently: every consumer-held artifact is digest-verified, and a republished image is a new digest. The attack image’s recipe version MUST bump for each republish, so the realized identity re-keys; between publish days the catalog deliberately drifts from upstream feeds (the manifest records what shipped). Moving a fleet forward is the explicit act: `images refresh <name>`, or regenerating the pin file.


# Example Ranges – Inspect Ranges

## Overview

The `examples/` directory holds ranges translated faithfully from published definitions, then promoted to built, verified, solved ranges: recipes realize the declared guest content, the build’s behavioral checks prove each challenge (the reference chain scores 1.0, insufficient and forged attempts score 0.0), and a real `inspect eval` solves each range through its declared foothold. Every example carries its upstream provenance (`source.md`, vendored `upstream/`, per-field tags in `range.yaml`), its unrealized remainder (`deferred.yaml`), and a realization record (`notes.md`).

| Example | Upstream | The chain | Foothold |
|----|----|----|----|
| `vulhub-zabbix` | Vulhub (CVE-2016-10134) | unauthenticated SQLi, admin session, Zabbix script execution on server and agent | dedicated attack box |
| `kypo-demo` | KYPO CRP demo (Masaryk) | port discovery, wordlist telnet guess, sudoers `less` escalation | the client host (assumed breach) |
| `cyris-basic` | CyRIS reference (JAIST) | weak-root-password privesc; firewall-policy recon; forensics triage of planted captures | the desktop host (assumed breach) |
| `mhbench-equifax-small` | MHBench (CMU) | CVE-2017-5638 Struts RCE, planted SSH-key pivot, four-database exfiltration | the standard attack box (catalog default) |

## What the examples demonstrate

- **kypo-demo** is the routed-topology reference: two subnets joined by a declared router, per-instance `variables:` resolving to defaults, a milestone ladder challenge, and the plant layer owning the flags (checked-in defaults never score).
- **cyris-basic** is the firewall-ACL reference: a plain-router guest carrying the upstream 25/53 forwarding rules, deterministic synthesized evidence artifacts (pcaps, log noise, a resident dummy process), and a weights-scored forensics challenge.
- **mhbench-equifax-small** is the scale and catalog reference: six targets, the attacker as the schema default (no `image:` line, the catalog’s `attack`), a real CVE entry asserted live at build, and coverage-scored exfiltration with source-bound pcap corroboration.
- **vulhub-zabbix** is the era-exact CVE reference: version-exact services compiled from canonical archives, with the patch dual (a defender removing the weakness) in its challenge set.

Each example’s `checks/<challenge-id>/{reference,insufficient,forged}.sh` trio runs at build against the captured artifacts; a build whose proof fails records a refused manifest, and no consumer can boot an unproven range.

## Running one

``` bash
$ cd examples/kypo-demo
$ inspect-ranges build          # realize + verify + prove (build egress required)
$ inspect eval my_task.py       # a task with sandbox=("range", "examples/kypo-demo/range.yaml")
```

Images resolve from the published catalog (see [Image Catalog](./catalog.html.md)); a connected machine needs no explicit pulls.


# Host Topology – Inspect Ranges

## Two topologies, one switch

The provider realizes ranges through one of two backends, selected by `INSPECT_RANGES_HOST`:

- **`local`** (the default): today’s co-resident path. The driver process renders the bundle and runs realization in-process; guests are reached directly over vsock. Nothing changes versus a pre-topology setup except that every sample now also holds a host lease (below).
- **`uds:<socket>`**: the separated topology on one host. A standing `inspect-ranges applier` process owns realization and teardown; the driver talks to it over a unix socket, and every guest operation relays through the same socket as an opaque byte stream. The driver still renders bundles (the compiler toolchain is driver-side) and still leases CIDs; the applier verifies the bundle digest and runs `up`.

``` bash
# terminal 1: the applier (one per host; it refuses to serve an unhealthy host)
inspect-ranges applier --socket /run/user/1000/ir-applier.sock

# terminal 2: evals through it
INSPECT_RANGES_HOST=uds:/run/user/1000/ir-applier.sock inspect eval my_task.py
```

Both backends behave identically at the eval surface: same sandboxes, same ops, same cleanup semantics. The separated topology exists so the process that parses attacker-influenced bytes can be isolated from the process holding credentials; on one host it buys crash independence (a dead driver no longer strands cleanup knowledge in a dead process) and is the stepping stone to real multi-host dispatch.

Keep socket paths short: `AF_UNIX` paths cap at about 107 bytes, so prefer `/run/user/<uid>/...` or a short `/tmp` directory over deeply nested trees.

## The lease contract

Every sample holds a **host lease**: an identity plus an absolute expiry, recorded in `leases.json` beside the CID registry under the shared state dir. The driver renews it at a third of the TTL (`INSPECT_RANGES_LEASE_TTL_S`, default 600 seconds); renewal is an on-disk compare-and-swap, so there is zero hot-path wire chatter. Release is destruction: a lease is removed only after a successful teardown, and a used host is never returned to a pool.

**The expiry-mid-sample policy, stated loudly: the reaper reclaims on expiry alone and never probes liveness.** A healthy sample never expires, because renewal is independent of sample activity; the only way to expire mid-sample is a dead or wedged driver, which is exactly what the reaper exists for. If a running sample’s lease is reclaimed anyway (forced expiry, operator intervention), the driver fails the sample loudly with `LeaseLostError` at its next operation rather than letting it limp along on a reclaimed host. There is no looks-alive grace period; adding one would reintroduce the dependence on driver liveness that leases exist to remove.

## Operating the reaper

`inspect-ranges reaper` is the independent cleanup process: fresh-process, on-disk only, never dependent on the original driver reaching its `finally`.

``` bash
inspect-ranges reaper                 # one sweep, exit 1 if any reclaim failed
inspect-ranges reaper --interval 60   # a long-lived daemon sweeping every minute
```

A sweep selects expired (and crashed-mid-reap) leases under the registry lock, re-checking expiry so a renewal that just landed spares its lease, marks them `reaping` (which makes any further renewal fail), tears each range down OUTSIDE the lock, and only after a successful teardown releases the CID lease, clears staging and ownership records, and removes the host lease last. A failed teardown frees nothing: the lease stays findable and the next sweep retries. For `uds:` leases the reaper tears down through the applier socket (which also releases the applier’s admission charge); if the applier is unreachable it falls back to direct teardown with a logged warning that a live applier’s charge leaks until restart.

`inspect-ranges doctor` reports lease health in its Host group, including an expired-leases hint that names the reaper.

## Operating the applier

`inspect-ranges applier --socket <path> [--state-dir <dir>] [--image-cache <dir>]` serves two planes on one 0600 socket (same-uid trust): the host plane (realize, teardown, heartbeat) and a per-guest byte relay. It runs the doctor readiness subset at startup and refuses to serve an unhealthy host.

Realize is gated: the requested bundle digest must match the lease’s rendered bundle (`EINVAL` otherwise), fetch grants must be empty (below), and the range’s declared resources are charged against the applier’s own admission gate, which refuses rather than queues: `EAGAIN` when the host is full right now (the driver respins), `ENOSPC` when the range alone exceeds the host (permanent). One realize per lease: a second realize on a live lease refuses `EBUSY` until teardown.

**Applier restart is a recorded v1 limitation**: the replay log, guest relay map, and admission charges live in process memory and die with it (logged loudly at startup when live leases exist). Running samples keep their VMs; their teardowns recover from disk (the driver’s teardown, the reaper, or `inspect sandbox cleanup range`), and new samples are served cleanly. When the applier is fully dead and a lease still exists, `inspect sandbox cleanup range` fails loudly by design (teardown for a leased project routes through the applier); recovery is reaper-only, via its direct-teardown fallback and the logged charge-leak warning.

## The grants convention

`realize` carries a list of fetch grants for image delivery. In v1 the only supported delivery is **pre-seeded**: the image cache on the host already holds the verified golden chain, and the grants list must be empty. A non-empty grants list refuses with `ENOTSUP` rather than silently ignoring it, so a deployment that expects granted-URL delivery fails at realize, not mid-boot. Granted-URL and registry delivery are the image-distribution growth path.

## What the isolation claim means

Every lease records an isolation claim, and the provider logs it once per sample acquisition. Both v1 backends claim **`isolation="shared"`**: one host’s kernel, device emulation, and caches are reused across samples, so a guest-to-host escape in one sample could reach another sample’s resources. The claim is honest labeling for the eval log, not a control. `isolation="instance"` (a fresh host per sample) arrives only with a real fleet provider; nothing in v1 pretends otherwise.

## Environment reference

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|----|----|----|
| `INSPECT_RANGES_HOST` | `local` | Backend selection: `local` (co-resident) or `uds:<socket>` (a running applier). |
| `INSPECT_RANGES_LEASE_TTL_S` | 600 | Host lease TTL in seconds; the driver renews at TTL/3. A dead driver’s sample becomes reclaimable one TTL after its last renewal. |
| `INSPECT_RANGES_HOST_CLASS` | `unspecified` | The host-class name recorded in lease host facts (declarations, never per-instance probes). |

The provider’s own knobs (concurrency, retries, image cache) are on the [Sandbox Provider](./provider.html.md) page and apply unchanged under either backend.


# Security – Inspect Ranges

## The threat model

Everything inside a range is assumed hostile: the attacker agent by design, targets once compromised. Containment is correspondingly strict, protecting two things that live outside the sample: the machine and credentials beyond the range, and the integrity of the sample’s score. The model assumes one sample per host instance, for the instance’s lifetime: a compromised host can persist across VM and container teardown, so a used host is never returned to a pool (the [lease contract](./topology.html.md#the-lease-contract) encodes this as release-is-destruction).

Escapes are treated as possible but unprofitable. An agent that escapes its VM gains an unprivileged, credential-free container; one that escapes that gains a dedicated instance holding no secrets and a sample that is simply discarded. Evidence streams off the instance continuously, so the record received before an escape cannot be rewritten afterward (see [Evidence](./evidence.html.md)).

## Three nested boundaries

The agent sits behind three boundaries, each independent of the last:

1.  **The VM boundary.** Every guest, including the attack box, is a hardware virtual machine. The escape surface is kept small and declared: virtual hardware is compiled explicitly per role, and the attack box sees only virtio disk, network, vsock, serial console, and entropy devices.
2.  **The range container.** Nearly all historical VM escapes break out through the device-emulation process and land here: an unprivileged container holding no credentials, with Docker’s default capabilities dropped (eight added back: `NET_ADMIN` plus the file-ownership and user-switching set that lets the VMMs run as non-root users), four device nodes (`/dev/kvm`, `/dev/net/tun`, `/dev/vhost-net`, `/dev/vhost-vsock`), and the standard seccomp and AppArmor profiles. The range’s bridges and firewall rules exist only inside this container’s network namespace, and teardown is the container lifecycle.
3.  **The instance.** Reaching the host from the container requires a second, unrelated exploit, and the host is a dedicated machine: even full compromise yields only the sample context, with the cloud hypervisor between it and everything else.

## Per-guest identity

An escape from one guest’s VMM should own nothing else, so no two VMMs share an identity:

- **QEMU guests** each run as their own unprivileged uid, derived from the guest’s leased vsock CID, with QEMU’s syscall sandbox on and the container’s AppArmor profile around the whole stack.
- **The attack box defaults to Cloud Hypervisor**, a smaller rust-vmm device model with no legacy hardware surface, started directly (no management daemon in its path) as its own unprivileged per-guest uid with no capabilities and Cloud Hypervisor’s default seccomp filter. The binary and its firmware are sha256-pinned into the range image. See [Virtual machine monitors](./provider.html.md#virtual-machine-monitors).

Graded honestly, boundary strength orders rust-vmm above QEMU/KVM, which has a long device-emulation CVE history. The Cloud Hypervisor attack box is a gate, not a tier upgrade: compromising targets is the sanctioned objective, so a successful agent reaches QEMU through any rooted target regardless of what the attack box runs on. What it buys is closing the quiet path, an escape launched from the one guest where the agent has root and full tooling from the first prompt, forcing escape attempts through observable, evidence-producing compromise work first.

## The control plane is not a network

Guest control rides virtio-vsock, not a management network. The rules:

- Guests get lab-segment NICs only: no management NIC, no management subnet for in-range software to discover, firewall, or pivot through.
- The plane is strictly connect-from-host: the in-guest daemon accepts connections only from the host, and no host-side `AF_VSOCK` listeners exist for a compromised guest to dial.
- Cloud Hypervisor guests are reached over the VMM’s hybrid-vsock Unix socket, and every dialer checks the socket peer’s credentials against the VMM’s uid before sending a byte.
- Everything received over the channel comes from guests the agent may have compromised and is treated as untrusted input: strict schema validation, reader-side byte caps, and tamper verdicts for protocol violations an honest endpoint cannot produce (see [the retry contract](./provider.html.md#the-retry-contract)).

In the other direction, in-range defenders can detect everything the agent transmits (that is realism, not a leak), but they cannot observe the agent’s interior, connect to it (standard images ship zero network listeners), or reach the channel controlling it.

## Network containment: three authorities

Scenario networking and operator containment are different authorities, each with its own owner:

1.  **Scenario intent** (the definition): `mode` and `egress` describe the scenario, and the compiler realizes them in guest configs and router ACLs.
2.  **Mutable in-range state** (run time): routers are ordinary guests and their firewall rulesets are scenario state. Compromising a router and rewriting its rules is legitimate agent behavior, not a containment event, so nothing operator-relevant may depend on in-guest rules.
3.  **Deployment-enforced external containment** (the authority that survives compromise): hypervisor-side firewall invariants in the range’s network namespace, outside every guest, plus the instance’s own network policy. These are compiled from deployment policy, not from the scenario: a definition may request external capabilities, and the deployment grants or rejects them. No schema field weakens operator containment.

## Containment is proved, not assumed

A range that carries [behavioral checks](./building.html.md#behavioral-checks) proves its containment at build time. Before the checks, the proof boot runs the `conformance` stage: a shared-segment target TCP-sweeps the attacker expecting zero open ports, and the attacker verifies that no undeclared management endpoint answers on its segments. Any finding refuses the manifest exactly like a failed check, so an uncontained range is never consumable.

The stage’s scope limits, recorded plainly: the sweep is TCP only (ports 1-1024 plus a high-port sample), foothold ranges skip it (the agent lands on a declared host whose services legitimately answer), and a range without behavioral checks has no proof boot, so it gets no conformance stage either.

## Score integrity: detection over prevention

Streaming preserves the evidence record but does not by itself detect an escape, so each goal type is scored against proof the agent cannot fabricate, and detection-type goals consume coverage watermarks rather than trusting exported content (see [Challenges](./challenges.html.md) and [Evidence](./evidence.html.md)). An escaped agent can invalidate its sample; it cannot silently falsify it. Score integrity rests on that detection, not on the boundaries being unbreakable.

## Topologies and credentials

The co-resident topology (the `local` backend) puts the driver, with its model API credentials, on the same host as the range: it is for development and trusted runs, and its credentials must be scoped and revocable (per-run model keys, no long-lived cloud credentials). The separated topology (`uds:`) isolates the process that parses attacker-influenced bytes from the process holding credentials and is the preferred configuration where the agent is genuinely untrusted; see [Host Topology](./topology.html.md).

Both v1 backends record `isolation="shared"` in the eval log: one host’s kernel, device emulation, and caches are reused across samples, so the one-sample-per-instance posture above is a deployment property, not something v1 enforces. The claim is honest labeling; `isolation="instance"` arrives only with a real fleet provider.

For untrusted-model runs, point the eval log directory or `INSPECT_RANGES_EVIDENCE_SINK` at off-instance storage, since instance-local evidence does not survive instance compromise ([deployment guidance](./evidence.html.md#deployment-guidance-store-side-prevention)); `inspect-ranges doctor` warns when evidence resolves to local storage.


# inspect-ranges applier – Inspect Ranges

Serve realize/teardown/heartbeat and the guest relay for driver processes on this host.

Runs the doctor-readiness subset at startup and refuses to serve unhealthy. A restart loses the replay log, relay map, and admission charges (recorded v1 limitation); disk-driven teardown (the reaper, `inspect-ranges down`) is the recovery.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges applier [OPTIONS]
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--socket` | path | Unix socket to serve on (created 0600 in a 0700 directory). | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--state-dir` | path | Project state directory (default: the shared inspect-ranges state dir). | None |
| `--image-cache` | path | N/A | None |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |


# inspect-ranges build – Inspect Ranges

Build PATH (default `.`): realize, verify, capture, and prove the range’s declared guest content.

The build boots an egress-enabled variant of the range (runtime isolation is untouched), runs each host’s `provisioning` steps in declaration order, verifies every declared service and vulnerability against the live guests, captures each provisioned guest as a realized image, runs any declared behavioral checks against the captured artifacts, and records the build manifest that `plan`/`render`/`up`/the provider consume. Rebuilds are incremental per guest; an unchanged range is a cached no-op. `--keep` preserves the running range for diagnosis (and captures nothing). Full reference: the Building Ranges docs page.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges build [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--image-cache` | path | Image cache used for golden resolution. | None |
| `--recipe-cache` | path | Recipe cache for the resolution fallback after ./recipes/. | None |
| `--cid-base` | integer range (`3` and above) | First vsock CID (plan-time input; realizer batteries use 3000+). | `3` |
| `--keep` | boolean | Keep the built range running for inspection (success or failure); tear down with `inspect-ranges down`. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--uplink-network` | text | Docker network build-time egress masquerades onto (created when absent). | `ir-uplink` |
| `--build-nameserver` | text | Resolver handed to build guests (fleets forcing DNS through a VPC resolver are the norm, not the exception). | None |
| `--build-cache` | path | Builds cache where the range’s manifest lives. | None |
| `--reverify` | boolean | Boot and verify in full even when every build key matches the recorded manifest. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--readiness-timeout` | float | N/A | `300.0` |
| `--settle-probe` | text | Hostname each guest must resolve before its first recipe runs; pass ‘off’ to skip the gate (fleets whose resolver answers only internal names). | None |
| `--settle-timeout` | float | Seconds to wait for the settle probe per guest. | None |
| `--recipe-budget` | float | Whole-entrypoint budget per provisioning step, in seconds. | `1800.0` |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |

# inspect-ranges evidence – Inspect Ranges

Work with evidence locations (see design/inspect-ranges/evidence-v1.md).

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges evidence [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

#### Subcommands

|  |  |
|----|----|
| [verify](#inspect-ranges-evidence-verify) | Replay the hash chains at LOCATION and name the first break. |

## inspect-ranges evidence verify

Replay the hash chains at LOCATION and name the first break.

LOCATION is a local directory or an `s3://bucket/prefix` evidence location (S3 credentials follow standard AWS resolution). Exits 0 when every writer replays cleanly, 1 on any break or when no manifests exist. An unsealed writer is reported loudly but is not itself a break unless a binding was supplied for it (the lifecycle seals on finalize and on reap, where reap-sealing is done by whichever party reaches the abandoned record: the surviving driver at teardown, or the reaper and `cli_cleanup` for a dead driver; unsealed-at-rest means none of them happened). With `--expect-seal` the writer’s result carries the full detection claim; without it, internal consistency only.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges evidence verify [OPTIONS] LOCATION
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--shallow` | boolean | Replay manifests, chains, and seals only (skip fetching chunk bytes). | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the full report as JSON. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--expect-seal` | text | Externally-held seal digest to bind against (repeatable, one per writer). Without it, verification attests internal consistency only: the chain anchors everything at or below the seal, but a forged or absent seal, or a record transplanted from another location, is not detectable from the location alone. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |

## inspect-ranges images derive

Derive a daemon-baked golden from a digest-pinned vendor cloud image.

Offline derivation (Ubuntu noble vendor images in v1): verifies the vendor digest, bakes the pinned control daemon, disables ssh and the resolved stub listener, and records provenance beside the golden. Idempotent: re-running with the same inputs is a cache hit.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges images derive [OPTIONS] VENDOR
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--sha256` | text | Required digest pin for the vendor image (hex or sha256:-prefixed). | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--name` | text | Golden name (default: -golden). | None |
| `--image-cache` | path | Image cache the golden is derived into. | None |
| `--daemon-bundle` | path | Directory holding the daemon-bundle artifact and its daemon.json (default: the shared artifact cache; publish one with `inspect-ranges daemon-bundle`). | None |
| `--daemon-sha256` | text | Out-of-band pin for the daemon bundle digest (printed by `inspect-ranges daemon-bundle` at publish). Without it, the sidecar proves internal consistency only. | None |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |

## inspect-ranges images derive-windows

Install a sysprep’d Windows golden from digest-pinned eval media (windows-ad-v1).

A one-shot hardened range container runs the unattended install: viostor in WinPE, virtio guest tools and the vsock control daemon at first logon (compiled in-guest from the daemon bundle’s Windows sources), then `sysprep /generalize /shutdown`. Clones specialize per boot from the render-emitted unattend seed. Windows artifacts are LOCAL ONLY (recipes-not-images, the ratified posture); nothing Windows-derived publishes anywhere. Idempotent on the same media, daemon, and password pins.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges images derive-windows [OPTIONS] ISO
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--sha256` | text | Required digest pin for the Windows install ISO (hex or sha256:-prefixed). | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--virtio-iso` | path | The virtio-win driver ISO (viostor for WinPE, guest tools, the viosock driver). | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--virtio-sha256` | text | Required digest pin for the virtio-win ISO. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--name` | text | Golden name. | `windows-2022` |
| `--admin-password` | text | The golden’s built-in Administrator password (scenario content; the control plane is the vsock daemon as SYSTEM). Defaults to the documented constant. | None |
| `--image-cache` | path | Image cache the golden is installed into. | None |
| `--daemon-bundle` | path | Directory holding the daemon-bundle artifact (its windows/ sources compile in-guest). | None |
| `--daemon-sha256` | text | Out-of-band pin for the daemon bundle digest. | None |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |

## inspect-ranges images prune

Reclaim realized images no manifest references, plus capture temps and orphan sidecars; `--chains` extends to unreferenced goldens and vendor bases (pulled chains accounted exactly like built ones).

Build success already garbage-collects its own range (keeping the previous generation for rollback); prune covers the rest: generations stranded by refused manifests or crashes, ranges whose builds are gone, `.capturing` and `.pulling` temps, and sidecars whose image vanished. The chain tier’s liveness scan: a golden survives while any realized sidecar names it, any build manifest records it, or a live project boots it; a vendor base survives while any surviving golden’s provenance names it. Reports by default; `--yes` deletes. Refuses while registered projects exist unless `--force` (running projects’ files are excluded either way).

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges images prune [OPTIONS]
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--image-cache` | path | Image cache to prune. | None |
| `--build-cache` | path | Builds cache whose manifests define liveness. | None |
| `--yes` | boolean | Delete instead of reporting. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--force` | boolean | Prune even while registered projects exist (their referenced files are still excluded). | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--recipe-cache` | path | Recipe cache whose stranded pull stagings are reclaimed. | None |
| `--chains` | boolean | Also reclaim goldens and vendor bases nothing references (the distribution tier): eviction is by whole chain, never a backing out from under a dependent. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |

## inspect-ranges images pin

Write the fleet pin file (every catalog name’s current root digest); hosts consuming it via INSPECT_RANGES_PIN_FILE refuse a catalog that moved past the pinned state.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges images pin [OPTIONS]
```

#### Options

| Name     | Type    | Description                  | Default          |
|----------|---------|------------------------------|------------------|
| `--from` | text    | The catalog location to pin. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--out`  | path    | Pin file to write.           | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit.  | `Sentinel.UNSET` |


# inspect_ranges – Inspect Ranges

Load a definition with `load_range`, or get complete diagnostics (every error at once, with source positions and hints) from `validate_range`. Typed specs crossing a consumer boundary are re-checked with `revalidate_range`.

## Loading

### load_range

Load and validate a `range.yaml` file.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/schema.py#L199)

``` python
def load_range(path: Path) -> RangeSpec
```

`path` Path  
Path to the YAML file.

### validate_range

Validate a `range.yaml` file, reporting every detectable issue at once.

Unlike `load_range`, this never raises on invalid content: unreadable files (a directory, permissions, non-UTF-8 content), YAML syntax errors, structural schema violations, and semantic cross-reference problems all become [Issue](../reference/types.html.md#issue) entries with stable codes, source positions, and hints where available. Field-level structural errors suppress the cross-reference pass (reflected in `ValidationReport.semantic_checked`).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/schema.py#L135)

``` python
def validate_range(path: Path) -> ValidationReport
```

`path` Path  
Path to the YAML file.

### revalidate_range

Re-run full validation on a possibly mutated spec, returning a validated copy.

Spec models are mutable for flexible programmatic construction, so validity at construction is a point-in-time property. Consumer boundaries (the sandbox provider, the compiler) call this at handoff: the spec round-trips through `model_validate`, which catches semantic drift and type-unsafe mutations alike.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/schema.py#L222)

``` python
def revalidate_range(spec: RangeSpec) -> RangeSpec
```

`spec` [RangeSpec](../reference/types.html.md#rangespec)  
The spec to re-check (typically one received as sandbox configuration).

## Checks and Schema

### semantic_issues

Run every cross-reference check on a structurally valid spec, collecting all findings.

This is the single implementation of the semantic checks: [RangeSpec](../reference/types.html.md#rangespec) validation calls it (raising if any issue is found, so a freshly constructed spec is always consistent), and `validate_range` calls it via that same validation to report every issue at once.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L1093)

``` python
def semantic_issues(spec: RangeSpec) -> list[Issue]
```

`spec` [RangeSpec](../reference/types.html.md#rangespec)  
A structurally valid range definition.

### range_json_schema

Return the JSON Schema for `range.yaml` v0.1 (aliased field names, e.g. `from`).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/schema.py#L239)

``` python
def range_json_schema() -> dict[str, Any]
```


# inspect-ranges plan – Inspect Ranges

Resolve PATH (default `.`, a range directory or spec file) into its immutable plan.

Unsupported constructs fail here, at planning, with the same diagnostics as `validate`.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges plan [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--json` | boolean | Emit the plan as JSON. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--image-cache` | path | Image cache used for digest resolution. | None |
| `--cpu-model` | text | N/A | `host-passthrough` |
| `--cid-base` | integer range (`3` and above) | First vsock CID (plan-time input; realizer batteries use 3000+). | `3` |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |


# inspect-ranges reaper – Inspect Ranges

Reclaim expired host leases: teardown first, then CID and lease release.

Reclaims on expiry alone, never probing liveness: a healthy sample never expires because its driver renews independently. A failed teardown frees nothing and the lease stays findable for the next sweep. One-shot mode exits 1 if any teardown failed.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges reaper [OPTIONS]
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--state-dir` | path | Project state directory (default: the shared inspect-ranges state dir). | None |
| `--interval` | float range (`0` and above) | Seconds between sweeps; omitted means one sweep and exit. | None |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |


# inspect-ranges render – Inspect Ranges

Render PATH (default `.`, a range directory or spec file) into its realization bundle.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges render [OPTIONS] [PATH]
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--output`, `-o` | path | Bundle directory to write (must be empty or absent). | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--image-cache` | path | Image cache used for digest resolution. | None |
| `--cpu-model` | text | N/A | `host-passthrough` |
| `--cid-base` | integer range (`3` and above) | First vsock CID (plan-time input; realizer batteries use 3000+). | `3` |
| `--evidence-capture` | boolean | Render the evidence-capture sidecar (per-segment pcap; evidence-v1). | `False` |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |

# inspect_ranges.types – Inspect Ranges

The typed form of a range definition. A [RangeSpec](../reference/types.html.md#rangespec) is accepted directly as sandbox configuration (`sandbox=("range", RangeSpec(...))`), interchangeably with a `range.yaml` path. Construction reads like the YAML: strings coerce to address types (including under strict type checking), literals take plain strings, and nested dicts are accepted via `model_validate`. The one spelling divergence is [AclRule](../reference/types.html.md#aclrule)’s `from_=` keyword for the YAML `from:`.

Models validate fully at construction (structural and cross-reference checks) and stay mutable for programmatic building; every consumer boundary revalidates (see `revalidate_range`). See [Defining Ranges](../ranges.html.md) for a guided tour of the syntax.

## Range

### RangeSpec

A complete v0.1 range definition.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L909)

``` python
class RangeSpec(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`meta` [RangeMeta](../reference/types.html.md#rangemeta)  
Identity and provenance (the `range:` section in YAML; `meta=` in typed construction).

`networks` list\[[Network](../reference/types.html.md#network)\]  
Layer-2 segments.

`routers` list\[[Router](../reference/types.html.md#router)\]  
Gateway guests joining segments.

`hosts` list\[[Host](../reference/types.html.md#host)\]  
Target guests.

`attacker` [Attacker](../reference/types.html.md#attacker)  
The agent’s foothold.

`defense` [Defense](../reference/types.html.md#defense) \| None  
The range’s defensive posture (omitted means D0, no defenders).

`active_directory` [ActiveDirectory](../reference/types.html.md#activedirectory) \| None  
Active Directory identity data, for domain ranges.

`variables` dict\[str, [Variable](../reference/types.html.md#variable)\]  
Per-instance randomized values, referenced as `{name}` in YAML scalars (defaults substitute at load).

`foothold_guest` str  
The agent’s foothold guest name: the declared `attacker.host`, else the attack box itself. The one place the foothold-resolution rule lives; every consumer (registration, egress, disclosure, the patch re-run) reads it here.

### RangeMeta

Identity of the range.

Upstream provenance is a convention, not schema: record it in a `source.md` next to the `range.yaml`.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L83)

``` python
class RangeMeta(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Short identifier, e.g. `vulhub-zabbix`.

`schema_version` Literal\['0.1', '0.2', '0.3'\]  
Schema version this definition targets (omitted means `0.1`; `0.2` is the networking vocabulary, `0.3` adds guest configuration).

`description` str  
What the range is and why it exists.

## Guests

### Host

A target guest.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L682)

``` python
class Host(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Guest name, unique within the range.

`hostname` str \| None  
In-guest hostname, when it differs from `name`.

`fqdn` str \| None  
Fully qualified name, when the range’s DNS should serve it.

`os` [Os](../reference/types.html.md#os)  
Operating system.

`image` str  
Image reference the guest boots from.

`resources` [Resources](../reference/types.html.md#resources) \| None  
Sizing; omitted means backend defaults.

`vmm` Vmm  
Virtual machine monitor that runs this guest: `qemu` (default, via libvirt) or `cloud-hypervisor` (smaller device model; started directly, reached over its hybrid-vsock Unix socket).

`interfaces` list\[[Interface](../reference/types.html.md#interface)\]  
Network attachments (explicit; v0.1 has no implicit attachment).

`users` list\[[User](../reference/types.html.md#user)\]  
Local accounts (converged state; applied and verified at build).

`services` list\[[Service](../reference/types.html.md#service)\]  
The converged listening surface (assertions, verified at build).

`vulnerabilities` list\[[Vulnerability](../reference/types.html.md#vulnerability)\]  
Seeded exploitable weaknesses.

`misconfigurations` list\[[Misconfiguration](../reference/types.html.md#misconfiguration)\]  
Seeded misconfigurations.

`data` list\[[DataFile](../reference/types.html.md#datafile)\]  
Planted scenario files.

`defense` [HostDefense](../reference/types.html.md#hostdefense) \| None  
Per-host protection toggles.

`provisioning` list\[[ProvisioningStep](../reference/types.html.md#provisioningstep)\]  
Build-time recipe references, in order.

`roles` list\[str\]  
Functional role tags the build realizes (e.g. `domain-controller`, `dns`, `adcs`).

`scheduled_activity` list\[[ScheduledActivity](../reference/types.html.md#scheduledactivity)\]  
Recurring in-guest behavior simulation.

### Router

A gateway guest joining two or more networks, carrying the inter-segment ACL.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L651)

``` python
class Router(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Guest name, unique within the range.

`os` [Os](../reference/types.html.md#os) \| None  
Operating system, when the router is a full declared guest.

`image` str \| None  
Image reference; omitted means the backend’s default router appliance.

`resources` [Resources](../reference/types.html.md#resources) \| None  
Sizing; omitted means backend defaults.

`vmm` Vmm  
Virtual machine monitor that runs this guest: `qemu` (default, via libvirt) or `cloud-hypervisor` (smaller device model; started directly, reached over its hybrid-vsock Unix socket).

`interfaces` list\[[Interface](../reference/types.html.md#interface)\]  
One attachment per joined network (at least two).

`routes` list\[[Route](../reference/types.html.md#route)\]  
Static routes to segments reached through other routers.

`users` list\[[User](../reference/types.html.md#user)\]  
Local accounts (converged state; applied and verified at build).

`acl` list\[[AclRule](../reference/types.html.md#aclrule)\]  
Inter-segment policy enforced on this router (stateful; endpoints may be routed, not only attached). EMPTY means a plain router (everything forwards, the KYPO/CyRIS pure-router shape); declaring ANY rule flips the router to default-drop, forwarding only the declared allows plus established/related.

### Attacker

The agent’s foothold: either a dedicated attack box or an existing host.

Declare `host` to start on a declared host (assumed breach), or `interfaces` (plus optionally `name`, `image`, `resources`) to boot a dedicated attack box.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L737)

``` python
class Attacker(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Attack box guest name (ignored when `host` is set).

`host` str \| None  
Name of a declared host to use as the foothold instead of a dedicated box.

`image` str \| None  
Attack box image; omitted means the backend’s standard attack image (the catalog’s `attack`: the kali-class toolset image published under the org). Declare an image to opt out.

`resources` [Resources](../reference/types.html.md#resources) \| None  
Attack box sizing.

`vmm` Vmm \| None  
Attack box virtual machine monitor (see `Host.vmm`); unset, a dedicated attack box resolves to `cloud-hypervisor` at planning (unlike hosts and routers, which default to `qemu`). With `host` set, the foothold host’s own `vmm` applies and declaring one here is refused.

`interfaces` list\[[Interface](../reference/types.html.md#interface)\] \| None  
Attack box network attachments (required unless `host` is set).

`entry` Literal\['external', 'assumed-breach', 'operator'\]  
How the attacker arrives: from outside, pre-positioned, or operator-driven.

`egress` Literal\['none', 'open'\] \| [EgressPolicy](../reference/types.html.md#egresspolicy)  
Attacker-reachable egress from the range: `none` (default), `open`, or a scoped allowlist. Attacker egress composes ahead of network egress: `none` drops the attacker’s flows even on a network with an allowlist.

### Os

Guest operating system.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L328)

``` python
class Os(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`type` Literal\['linux', 'windows'\]  
OS family.

`distro` str \| None  
Linux distribution, e.g. `ubuntu-20.04`.

`version` str \| None  
Windows version, e.g. `server-2019`.

### Resources

Backend-neutral guest sizing.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L341)

``` python
class Resources(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`cpus` int  
Virtual CPU count.

`memory_mb` int  
Memory in MiB.

`disk_gb` int \| None  
Disk size in GiB, when the image default is not enough.

## Guest Content

### User

A local account on a guest.

Scenario credentials are scenario content and belong in the definition in plaintext; per-sample proof material (flags, canaries) never appears here. Domain accounts live in `active_directory`, not on hosts.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L354)

``` python
class User(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Account name.

`password` str \| None  
Password, when the scenario fixes one.

`groups` list\[str\]  
Local group memberships.

`note` str \| None  
Free-text intent, e.g. why the account exists or what makes it interesting.

### Credentials

A credential pair a service accepts.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L373)

``` python
class Credentials(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`user` str  
Account name.

`password` str  
Password.

### Service

An assertion about a guest’s converged listening surface.

Services are declarations, never an install language: the build satisfies them (via a provisioning recipe, content baked into the image, or a checkpoint) and verifies them before the range ships. Installation itself belongs in `provisioning`.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L383)

``` python
class Service(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Service name, unique on the host (vulnerabilities reference it).

`port` int \| None  
Listening port, when fixed.

`version` str \| None  
Expected version, when the scenario depends on it.

`package` str \| None  
The dpkg package that embodies the service, for build-time version verification when the listening process cannot attribute it (e.g. a PHP frontend served by apache: `package: zabbix-frontend-php`).

`credentials` [Credentials](../reference/types.html.md#credentials) \| None  
Credentials the service accepts, when scenario-relevant.

`note` str \| None  
Free-text detail.

### Vulnerability

A seeded exploitable weakness on a guest.

Exploitable vulnerabilities and misconfigurations are distinct lists because real intrusions lean heavily on the second; the list itself is the classification.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L408)

``` python
class Vulnerability(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`id` str  
Stable identifier, ours (e.g. `weak-telnet-password`, `adcs-esc1`).

`cve` str \| None  
CVE identifier, when one applies.

`service` str \| None  
The host service this weakness lives in, by `services[].name`.

`description` str  
What the weakness is and how it is reachable.

### Misconfiguration

A seeded misconfiguration on a guest (weak policy, dangerous sudoers line, disabled protection).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L427)

``` python
class Misconfiguration(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`id` str  
Stable identifier, ours.

`description` str  
What is misconfigured and why it matters.

### DataFile

A file planted on a guest as scenario content.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L437)

``` python
class DataFile(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`path` str  
Absolute in-guest path.

`description` str \| None  
What the file represents.

`sensitive` bool  
Whether the file is a scenario target (e.g. data worth exfiltrating).

`contents` str \| None  
Small inline contents; larger content is build material referenced by provisioning.

### ProvisioningStep

A build-time recipe reference, applied in list order.

Recipes run at build time and never per sample; their output is captured into images and checkpoints. The recipe language itself is deliberately out of the definition: a step names a recipe and its inputs, nothing more.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L466)

``` python
class ProvisioningStep(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`recipe` str  
Recipe reference, e.g. `P4T12ICK.ludus_ar_windows` or `scripts/promote-forest`.

`version` str \| None  
Recipe version, recorded in the build manifest.

`vars` dict\[str, str \| int \| bool\]  
Inputs passed to the recipe.

### ScheduledActivity

Recurring in-guest behavior, simulating users or defenders (bot scripts, scheduled tasks).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L482)

``` python
class ScheduledActivity(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`script` str  
Behavior reference, e.g. `asrep_roasting.ps1` or a recipe-style name.

`schedule` str \| None  
When it runs, when the scenario fixes it (e.g. a cron expression or an interval).

`user` str \| None  
The account the activity runs as, when scenario-relevant (e.g. for token-theft surface).

`note` str \| None  
Free-text intent.

### Variable

A named per-instance value: drawn fresh for each generated instance, with a required default.

Definitions reference variables as `{name}` in YAML scalars; loading substitutes the defaults before validation, so a whole-scalar reference takes the variable’s typed value (`port: "{{telnet_port}}"` validates as an integer) and embedded references interpolate as text. Required defaults mean every definition always validates and realizes concretely: v1 semantics ARE defaults-resolution (linux-examples-v1), per-sample secrets are the challenge plant layer’s job, and a per-instance generation layer that redraws non-secret values is deferred (see linux-examples-v1-parked-decisions.md). Python authors draw values and construct concretely instead of using references.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L498)

``` python
class Variable(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`default` str \| int \| bool  
The value used until generation draws one, and the fallback definition of the variable’s type.

`type` Literal\['text', 'password', 'port', 'int', 'choice'\] \| None  
What to draw, when generation lands; omitted means the default’s own type.

`min` int \| None  
Lower bound for numeric draws.

`max` int \| None  
Upper bound for numeric draws.

`choices` list\[str\] \| None  
The candidate set, for `type: choice`.

`description` str \| None  
What the variable controls.

## Defense

### Defense

The range’s defensive posture, on the D0 (no defenders) to D5 (adaptive defender) spectrum.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L814)

``` python
class Defense(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`tier` Literal\['D0', 'D1', 'D2', 'D3', 'D4', 'D5'\]  
How much the environment fights back: D0 none, D1 static hardening, D2 passive detection, D3 scripted response, D4 autonomous EDR, D5 adaptive.

`description` str \| None  
What the posture consists of.

`telemetry` list\[[Telemetry](../reference/types.html.md#telemetry)\]  
Telemetry flows, when the range records or forwards signals.

### HostDefense

Per-host protection toggles (typed knowns; extended when evidence forces).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L453)

``` python
class HostDefense(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`defender` bool \| None  
Microsoft Defender on or off.

`firewall` bool \| None  
Host firewall on or off.

`windows_update` bool \| None  
Windows Update on or off.

### Telemetry

One telemetry flow: which guest’s signals reach which sink.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L801)

``` python
class Telemetry(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`source` str  
The observed guest, by name.

`collector` str  
What gathers the signals, e.g. `Sysmon/WinEventLog` or an agent name.

`sink` str  
Where the signals land: a declared guest name, or a description of an external sink.

## Active Directory

### ActiveDirectory

Range-scoped Active Directory identity data.

Identity is declared here, not on hosts, because accounts exist in the domain. The build realizes it (promotion, joins, account and ACL seeding) and captures the converged result; see `design/inspect-ranges/range-build.md`.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L896)

``` python
class ActiveDirectory(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`forest` str  
Forest root domain name.

`domains` list\[[AdDomain](../reference/types.html.md#addomain)\]  
The forest’s domains.

### AdDomain

One domain in the forest.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L874)

``` python
class AdDomain(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
DNS name of the domain.

`netbios` str  
NetBIOS name.

`dc` str  
The domain controller, by declared guest name.

`parent` str \| None  
Parent domain name, for child domains.

`users` list\[[AdUser](../reference/types.html.md#aduser)\]  
Domain accounts of note.

`acls` list\[[AdAcl](../reference/types.html.md#adacl)\]  
Seeded ACL-abuse edges.

### AdUser

A domain account.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L855)

``` python
class AdUser(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
sAMAccountName.

`password` str \| None  
Password, when the scenario fixes one.

`groups` list\[str\]  
Group memberships.

`spns` list\[str\]  
Service principal names (kerberoastable surface).

`note` str \| None  
Free-text intent, e.g. what makes the account interesting.

### AdAcl

One seeded ACL-abuse edge: `principal` holds `right` over `target`.

Principals and targets are names as AD knows them (users, groups, OUs, or computer objects) and are not cross-validated against declared users this round.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L839)

``` python
class AdAcl(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`principal` str  
Who holds the right.

`right` [AdRight](../reference/types.html.md#adright)  
The right held.

`target` str  
What the right applies to.

### AdRight

Seeded AD ACL rights (the vocabulary observed in surveyed ranges; extended when evidence forces).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L827)

``` python
AdRight = Literal[
    "GenericAll",
    "GenericWrite",
    "WriteDacl",
    "WriteOwner",
    "ForceChangePassword",
    "SelfMembership",
    "AddMember",
]
```

## Networks

### Network

A layer-2 segment with its addressing and egress posture.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L254)

``` python
class Network(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Segment name, unique within the range.

`cidr` [AnyIPNetwork](../reference/types.html.md#anyipnetwork)  
Subnet, e.g. `10.10.10.0/24` (IPv6 subnets are gated by `ipv6-not-realized` until realization lands).

`mode` Literal\['isolated', 'nat', 'routed'\]  
Egress posture: `isolated` (no egress), `nat`, or `routed`.

`dhcp` bool  
Whether guests on this network get addresses via DHCP (default: static).

`dns` [DnsConfig](../reference/types.html.md#dnsconfig) \| None  
DNS behavior on this network.

`gateway` str \| None  
The router that is this network’s default gateway; required only when more than one router attaches (a single attached router is elected implicitly).

`egress` [EgressPolicy](../reference/types.html.md#egresspolicy) \| None  
Scoped egress allowlist; only meaningful with `mode: nat` (the hypervisor NATs exactly these flows out).

### Interface

A guest’s attachment to a network.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L308)

``` python
class Interface(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`network` str  
Name of a declared network.

`ip` [AnyIPAddress](../reference/types.html.md#anyipaddress) \| None  
Static address within the network’s subnet; omitted means IPAM-allocated.

### DnsConfig

Per-network DNS, as a union of the shapes real ranges need.

`records` serves name-based discovery on flat networks; `nameservers` points guests at external resolvers; `authoritative` names guests (e.g. domain controllers) that are the network’s DNS servers, optionally chaining to `forwarder`.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L115)

``` python
class DnsConfig(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`records` list\[[DnsRecord](../reference/types.html.md#dnsrecord)\] \| None  
Name records served by the range for this network.

`nameservers` list\[[AnyIPAddress](../reference/types.html.md#anyipaddress)\] \| None  
External resolvers handed to guests.

`authoritative` list\[str\] \| None  
Guests that act as this network’s DNS servers, in resolution order.

`forwarder` [AnyIPAddress](../reference/types.html.md#anyipaddress) \| None  
Upstream forwarder for the authoritative chain.

### DnsRecord

A name record served on a network.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L99)

``` python
class DnsRecord(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`name` str  
Hostname to resolve.

`ip` [AnyIPAddress](../reference/types.html.md#anyipaddress) \| None  
Address, when not derivable from the named guest’s interface.

### EgressPolicy

A scoped egress allowlist: exactly what may leave, nothing else.

Entries are `CIDR[:proto/port]` (a bare address is its `/32`; omitting the service allows all traffic to the CIDR) or `FQDN:proto/port`. FQDN entries are in the vocabulary but gated by `egress-fqdn-not-realized` until their realization lands (networking-v0.2 §3).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L203)

``` python
class EgressPolicy(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`allow` list\[str\]  
Allowlist entries, e.g. `198.51.100.7:tcp/443`, `0.0.0.0/0:udp/123`; empty allows nothing.

### Route

A static route on a router, for traffic to segments it reaches through another router.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L630)

``` python
class Route(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`to` [AnyIPNetwork](../reference/types.html.md#anyipnetwork)  
Destination subnet.

`via` [AnyIPAddress](../reference/types.html.md#anyipaddress)  
Next hop; must be an address inside one of the router’s attached networks.

### AclRule

One ordered rule on a router, carrying exactly one of `allow:` or `deny:`.

Rules evaluate first-match in list order against new connections `from` one endpoint `to` another; anything no rule matches is dropped (default-deny), and return traffic of allowed flows always passes (stateful). Endpoints are a network name, a guest name (resolved to its allocated addresses at plan time), or a CIDR (`/32` for a literal host, `0.0.0.0/0` for any). `deny` exists for carve-outs inside a broader allow. In typed construction the source field is spelled `from_` (the YAML surface keeps `from:`).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L563)

``` python
class AclRule(_StrictModel)
```

#### Attributes

`from_` str  
Source endpoint: network name, guest name, or CIDR (`from:` in YAML; `from_=` in typed construction).

`to` str  
Destination endpoint: network name, guest name, or CIDR.

`allow` list\[str\] \| None  
Services to allow, as `proto/port`, `proto/lo-hi`, or `icmp` entries, e.g. `tcp/5432`, `tcp/1-65535`; empty allows nothing.

`deny` list\[str\] \| None  
Services to drop at this point in the rule order (same entry syntax as `allow`).

### AnyIPAddress

Either address family. IPv6 values validate structurally but are rejected by the `ipv6-not-realized` gate until their realization lands (networking-v0.2 §4).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L27)

``` python
AnyIPAddress = IPv4Address | IPv6Address
```

### AnyIPNetwork

Either address family. IPv6 values validate structurally but are rejected by the `ipv6-not-realized` gate until their realization lands (networking-v0.2 §4).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/types.py#L30)

``` python
AnyIPNetwork = IPv4Network | IPv6Network
```

## Diagnostics

### Issue

One problem found in a range definition.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/_diagnostics.py#L47)

``` python
class Issue(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`code` str  
Stable kebab-case identifier, e.g. `undeclared-network`.

`severity` Severity  
Whether the issue blocks use of the spec.

`path` tuple\[PathElement, ...\]  
Location within the spec, e.g. `("networks", 0, "cidr")`.

`line` int \| None  
1-based source line, when the YAML parse can supply it.

`col` int \| None  
1-based source column, when the YAML parse can supply it.

`message` str  
What is wrong.

`hint` str \| None  
Actionable suggestion, e.g. a did-you-mean or where deferred content goes.

`path_str` str  
The path rendered as `networks[0].cidr`, or `(root)` for the document root.

### ValidationReport

Every issue found in one `range.yaml`, with rendering helpers.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/_diagnostics.py#L88)

``` python
class ValidationReport(BaseModel)
```

#### Attributes

`file` str  
The validated file path, as given.

`issues` list\[[Issue](../reference/types.html.md#issue)\]  
All issues found, in source order where positions are known.

`semantic_checked` bool  
False when structural errors prevented the cross-reference checks from running.

`spec` Any \| None  
The validated [RangeSpec](../reference/types.html.md#rangespec) when the file is valid, for callers that need it.

`valid` bool  
True when no error-severity issues were found.

#### Methods

render  
Render the report as aligned, human-readable text (warnings do not invalidate).

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/_diagnostics.py#L110)

``` python
def render(self) -> str
```

to_json  
Return the report as JSON-serializable data with stable field names.

[Source](https://github.com/meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ranges/blob/d3fa0e1f34526ceb86120496aca67d4787321315/src/inspect_ranges/_diagnostics.py#L144)

``` python
def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]
```


# inspect-ranges up – Inspect Ranges

Realize a rendered BUNDLE into a running, ready range.

Verifies every manifest digest before acting (tampered or incomplete bundles refuse), brings up the hardened range container on the bundle’s own compose project, boots every guest per `boot.json`, and waits on every readiness probe. The hardened range image is required; there is no bypass.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges up [OPTIONS] [BUNDLE]
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--from-spec` | path | Render SPEC into a temporary bundle first, then apply it (composition sugar; the applier still consumes only the verified bundle). | None |
| `--project` | text | Compose project name (default: ir--). | None |
| `--image-cache` | path | N/A | None |
| `--cid-base` | integer range (`3` and above) | First vsock CID when rendering –from-spec (plan-time input). | `3` |
| `--readiness-timeout` | float | N/A | `300.0` |
| `--keep` | boolean | Keep a failed range running for inspection instead of tearing it down. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--uplink-network` | text | Deployment-supplied uplink network, for ranges that request egress. | None |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |


# inspect-ranges validate – Inspect Ranges

Validate `range.yaml` files against schema v0.1 (default: the current directory’s).

Reports every detectable issue in each file at once, with source positions and hints. Each PATH may be a spec file or a range directory. Exits with status 1 if any file is invalid.

#### Usage

``` text
inspect-ranges validate [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...
```

#### Options

| Name | Type | Description | Default |
|----|----|----|----|
| `--json` | boolean | Emit one JSON report per file instead of text. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
| `--help` | boolean | Show this message and exit. | `Sentinel.UNSET` |
